entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen13410" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13411" type="x-p"/> By Eglah his wide - The Targum, Jarchi, and others, maintain that this was Michal, the daughter of Saul; but this does not well agree with <reference osisRef="2Sam.6.23">2Sam 6:23</reference> : Michal had no child to the day of her death. Yet she might have had a child before the time that is mentioned above.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen13413" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13414" type="x-p"/> Nine - There are thirteen if we count the four sons of Bath-sheba, and nine without them; and in the second book of Samuel there are eleven, reckoning the above four, and without them only seven. In the book of Samuel probably only those who were alive were reckoned, while the author of the Chronicles comprises those also who were dead in this enumeration. Jarchi supposes that the duplicate Elishama and Eliphelet are those which increase the regular number seven to nine; and that the dead without posterity, as well as the living, are mentioned to increase the number of David's descendants; for, says he, the whole book is written for the honor of David and his seed.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 16</hi> <div eID="gen13415" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13416" type="x-p"/> Zedekiah his son - If this be the same who was the last king of Judah, before the captivity, the word son must be taken here to signify successor; for it is certain that Zedekiah was the successor of Jeconiah, and that Zedekiah was the son of Josiah, and not of Jehoiakim.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 17</hi> <div eID="gen13416" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13417" type="x-p"/> The sons of Jeconiah - Jeremiah has said (<reference osisRef="Jer.22.30">Jer 22:30</reference>) that Jeconiah, or, as he calls him, Coniah, should be childless; but this must refer to his posterity being deprived of the throne, and indeed thus the prophet interprets it himself: For no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah. <div eID="gen13417" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13418" type="x-p"/> Assir - Salathiel was not the son of Assir, but of Jeconiah, <reference osisRef="Mat.1.12">Mat 1:12</reference>. Who then was Assir? Possibly nobody; for as the Hebrew אסר assir signifies a prisoner, it may be considered as an epithet of Jeconiah, who we know was a very long time prisoner in Babylon. See <reference osisRef="2Kgs.24.15">2Kgs 24:15</reference> and Calmet.
